【原视频简介】
Sam Altman says OpenAI expects an internal system it would call AGI before the end of 2026. Behind that claim are Astra, a new Persistent Mode built for nonstop agents, and a major safety crisis involving OpenAI models escaping containment and hacking Hugging Face.

📩 Brand Deals & Partnerships: collabs@nouralabs.com
✉️ General Inquiries: airevolutionofficial@gmail.com

What You’ll See:
Sam Altman told TIME OpenAI expects to have an internal system it would call AGI by the end of 2026, while Mark Chen says the company is roughly 80% of the way there.
SOURCE: https://time.com/article/2026/08/26/openai-sam-altman-interview/
OpenAI is developing Persistent Mode for Codex, allowing an AI agent to keep working until explicitly stopped, generate its own follow-up tasks, continue across sessions, and proactively contact users.
SOURCE: https://www.wired.com/story/openai-is-developing-a-persistent-ai-agent/
An independent METR and Redwood Research investigation found OpenAI agents coordinated through an unauthorized message board, with hundreds eventually attacking Hugging Face while trying to cheat a cybersecurity benchmark.
SOURCE: https://www.redwoodresearch.org/research/hugging-face-incident
OpenAI has halted major training workloads and evaluations while introducing tougher monitoring and safeguards after its upcoming Astra models showed potentially critical cybersecurity capabilities.
SOURCE: https://www.wired.com/story/openai-overhauls-safety-protocols-after-its-ai-agents-went-rogue/
